findings.message: SPDX header declares 'Apache-2.0' (an OSS grant) while the repository's true license (/LICENSE) is Proprietary — 'NO LICENSE GRANTED', All rights reserved (loopzero.example 2026). Git history shows in-repo authorship (author paulohenriquevn + LoopZero <admin@loopzero.example>, commit subjects 'migrate bash -> Go' / 'Go port') — not third-party import — so this is a systemic internal SPDX-vs-LICENSE inconsistency, not plagiarism. A proprietary product publicly asserting an Apache-2.0 grant on every source file creates legal ambiguity about what rights recipients actually have.
findings.remediation: Align the file header with the true license (compliance-only): replace the Apache-2.0 SPDX tag with the proprietary notice (e.g. '// SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary' + the loopzero.example copyright) repo-wide, OR relicense the repository to Apache-2.0 if an OSS grant is actually intended. NEVER rewrite git history to conceal the prior state.

findings.message: Uses the legacy filepath.Walk(dir, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error)) instead of the modern filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error)) (Go 1.16+). WalkDir avoids a per-file os.Lstat (it passes an fs.DirEntry), so it is the current house idiom. Same-suite inconsistency, not a defect: 10 gates use Walk, ~7 use WalkDir.
findings.remediation: Migrate the 10 Walk sites to filepath.WalkDir with an fs.DirEntry callback (use d.IsDir()/d.Type().IsRegular() and d.Info() when size/mode is needed), matching the WalkDir gates already in this package family.

findings.message: Blind guard — misapplied: the AGPL license-isolation gate fails OPEN on its own read/walk errors, so an unallowlisted AGPL import in an unreadable file (or a subtree behind a permission error) passes CI silently.

findings.message: The AGPL license-isolation gate's test suite never exercises the I/O-error path, so its fail-open behaviour on an unreadable file/dir is untested and unspecified. testing.md §4.1 requires a negative-case test that asserts what happens on an invalid/failing input; here the gate silently returns PASS on a WalkDir/ReadFile error (a security-relevant fail-open) and no test proves it, so a regression that widens the swallow would ship green.
findings.remediation: Add a negative-case test that makes a scanned dir/file unreadable (os.Chmod 0o000 as non-root, or a walk error) and asserts the gate does NOT silently PASS — pinning the intended fail-loud (or documented fail-open) contract per testing.md §4.1.

findings.message: SPDX header declares 'Apache-2.0' (an OSS grant) while the repository's true license (/LICENSE) is Proprietary — 'NO LICENSE GRANTED. All rights reserved', Copyright (c) 2026 loopzero.example. Git history (author paulohenriquevn + LoopZero <admin@loopzero.example>; commit subjects 'migrate <script>.sh to pure-Go gate' / 'refactor(loopzero-ops): relocate pkg/quality into cmd/loopzero-ops/internal') shows in-repo authorship of an internal bash→Go gate port — NOT a third-party import — so this is a systemic internal SPDX-vs-LICENSE inconsistency, not plagiarism. A proprietary product publicly asserting an Apache-2.0 grant on every quality-gate source file creates legal ambiguity about what rights recipients actually have. Same conflict class as the tranche-A files (rule_code 'license-header-conflict'); to be WONTFIX'd in bulk as a systemic founder decision.
findings.remediation: Align the file header with the true license (compliance-only): replace the Apache-2.0 SPDX tag with a proprietary notice (e.g. '// SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary' + the loopzero.example copyright) repo-wide, OR relicense the repository to Apache-2.0 if an OSS grant is actually intended. NEVER rewrite git history to conceal the prior state.

findings.message: 26 of the 116 queue files are not gofmt-clean under the module's declared toolchain (go 1.26.1 per go.mod). gofmt cleanliness is the canonical Go idiomaticity signal. Two failure classes: (a) genuine const/struct-field alignment drift (a longer identifier added/removed without re-aligning), and (b) doc-comment numbered-list re-indentation introduced by the go1.19+ gofmt comment formatter.
findings.remediation: Run gofmt -w (or go fmt ./...) over the 26 listed files and wire a gofmt/gofumpt check into task quality:gates so committed source stays gofmt-clean on the declared toolchain.

findings.evidence: gate walk now propagates error (fail-closed), commit 7c6b9df5
findings.message: The RBAC secrets/* blast-radius gate fails OPEN on I/O errors: the top-level Walk error is discarded and a clusterrole.yaml that cannot be opened is recorded only as a non-blocking WARN, so an unscannable ClusterRole template lets the gate PASS with an unguarded cluster-wide secrets grant undetected.
findings.remediation: Return the top-level Walk error rather than `_ =`, and treat a scanFile open/read error as a blocking failure (set Pass=false or return the error) — a security gate that cannot read a ClusterRole template must fail loud, not WARN-and-pass (rules/error-handling.md §2, Unbreakable Rule 8).

findings.message: Subprocess errors are formatted with %v instead of the wrapping verb %w, so the underlying error cannot be recovered via errors.Is/errors.As. The house idiom throughout this package family is %w (or a LoopZeroError with Cause), making these 5 sites inconsistent laggards.
findings.remediation: Change the error verb to %w for the err argument (e.g. fmt.Errorf("git diff failed: %w (stderr: %s)", err, stderr.String())) so subprocess failures unwrap; keep %s/%v only for non-error stderr/args operands.

findings.message: A single integer is parsed with fmt.Sscanf(parts[1], "%d", &lineno) and the returned (count, error) are BOTH discarded, instead of the idiomatic strconv.Atoi. On a non-numeric field lineno silently stays 0. This is the one outlier in the package family: every other parser here uses strconv.Atoi.
findings.remediation: Replace with `lineno, _ := strconv.Atoi(parts[1])` (git-grep output guarantees a numeric field, so dropping the error explicitly is fine) and add strconv to imports — matching the parsing idiom used everywhere else in the package.

findings.message: End-of-stream is detected by comparing the error MESSAGE string (err.Error() == "EOF" at :112, then strings.Contains(err.Error(), "EOF") at :117) instead of the idiomatic errors.Is(err, io.EOF). This is fragile (breaks if the wrapper changes the text) AND unsound: the strings.Contains(...,"EOF") fallback also matches io.ErrUnexpectedEOF (message 'unexpected EOF'), so a TRUNCATED YAML document is swallowed as a clean end-of-stream and silently returns partial CRDs.
findings.remediation: Replace both branches (:112 and :117) with a single `if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) { return out, nil }`; add errors and io to the import block. Handles direct + wrapped io.EOF and stops treating io.ErrUnexpectedEOF as success.

findings.message: validateWithPromtool interpolates a panel PromQL query into a YAML block scalar with a fixed 6-space indent on the FIRST line only; a multi-line Grafana `expr` therefore emits its 2nd+ lines at column 0, breaking the block-scalar indentation and making promtool report a parse error for a query that is actually valid (false positive).

findings.message: The gate directory (and its package) name `devpubliocidcredirectsyntax` is a typo of the canonical gate name. The convention across this tree is 'hyphenless run-together of the CLI gate name' — `dev-public-billing-portal-syntax` -> package `devpublicbillingportalsyntax`, `dev-public-env` -> `devpublicenv`. Applying that rule to this gate's own CLI name `dev-public-oidc-redirect-syntax` (registered verbatim in quality_registry.go:55 and flag.NewFlagSet 'dev-public-oidc-redirect-syntax') yields `devpublicoidcredirectsyntax`, but the folder is spelled `devpubli-o-c-idc...` (the 'c' and 'o' of 'publiC'+'Oidc' are transposed). Consequence for findability: the package cannot be located by its canonical run-together spelling, and it silently breaks the `devpublic*` prefix family it sits in (its two siblings spell 'devpublic' correctly). The package's own doc-comment betrays the intent — it says 'hermetic contract test for infra/tests/e2e/live/dev-public-oidc-redirect_test.sh' and cites 'canonical shape (devpublicbillingportalsyntax)'.
findings.remediation: Rename the directory and its package identifier from `devpubliocidcredirectsyntax` to `devpublicoidcredirectsyntax` (git mv the dir, update the `package` clause in check.go + check_test.go, and the import path + call sites in quality_gates_governance.go). This restores the hyphenless-CLI-name convention and the `devpublic*` prefix family so the package is findable by its canonical spelling.

findings.message: Template Method — missing_beneficial: the helm-template contract-gate shape (locate chart -> exec.LookPath("helm") advisory-fallthrough -> `helm template` render -> regexp match-count/assert) is reimplemented per-gate across >=3 assigned gates (esochartsanity, esocreationpolicy, day30day60cronjobs), with a byte-identical countMatches([]byte,string) int helper copied into two of them. A parallel bash-syntax contract-gate family (devpublicbillingportalsyntax, devpubliocidcredirectsyntax) copies an identical statAndRead/runQuiet + strict-mode/log/assert/exit-code/allowlist skeleton, which their own package docs describe as the 'canonical shape ... verbatim per M20/M22 blueprint ADR-D1'. Catalog smell 'algorithm steps duplicated with small variations -> Template Method / Strategy' (GoF Template Method: skeleton in a base, varying steps as hooks). A shared quality/scanhelpers Template Method (skeleton + per-gate assertion hook) would DRY the shared knowledge (helm-render+advisory-skip; bash -n+exit-code contract) that today diverges by copy. The deadlineratchet package in this same tranche proves the team DOES extract a Spec-parameterised shared algorithm when it chooses to. NON-BLOCKING suggestion; the cited blueprint ADR-D1 verbatim-copy decision may be a deliberate per-gate-isolation override.
findings.remediation: Extract a shared quality-gate Template Method (e.g. internal/quality/scanhelpers): a helm-render gate skeleton parameterised by the per-gate assertion set, and a bash-syntax gate skeleton (statAndRead/runQuiet/exit-code contract) parameterised by the domain regexes; keep the per-gate hook in each package. If the verbatim-copy is intentional per blueprint ADR-D1, cite that ADR in each gate to record the override.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: LOW/INFO design or perf observation (blind_guard/n_plus_one/dip_*/timeout/over_matching/folder-naming/repo_rewalk/ssot/predicate) on functionally-correct gate/seed code (full test GREEN). Design-preference or perf-nit, not a defect; documented tech-debt / conscious tradeoff. WONTFIX.
findings.message: The codebase declares a domain port for the shell/process boundary — pkg/shellrun.Runner (interface + a MockRunner test double) — and one gate consumes it correctly (gitdiff.RunGitDiff injects a shellrun.Runner, so its `git diff` path is exercised hermetically with shellrun.NewMock()). Every OTHER gate that shells out binds directly to the concrete os/exec.Command instead of the injected port: helm/diff/git/promtool/python3/bash are hardcoded. This is Dependency Inversion applied inconsistently at exactly the seam the codebase already abstracted — high-level gate logic depends on the low-level process concretion rather than the domain interface. The concrete cost is testability: gates that hardcode os/exec can only be integration-tested with the real binary present, so their tests fall back to t.Skip when it is absent — eroding the 'hermetic + offline' property the gate packages' own doc-comments promise (e.g. acyclicgraph 'hermetic + offline (no go list / build required)').
findings.remediation: Route external-process invocations through the existing pkg/shellrun.Runner port (inject a shellrun.Runner into each gate's Config as gitdiff does) so gate logic depends on the interface, not os/exec — then the exec path is exercised with shellrun.NewMock() and the t.Skip binary-gating is removed. Migrate incrementally, highest-leverage first (helm-template + diff gates), and add a code-quality check that new internal/quality gates do not import os/exec directly.

findings.message: The k6-load-rigor gate asserts 15+ distinct structural invariants (Phase 1-4: dropped_iterations `count<` vs `rate<` EC-2, L5 TestRun shape, pinned image, Prometheus RW, secretKeyRef, README per-level docs, gate wiring), yet the test suite exercises only the whole-file-missing failure and a real-repo PASS. No per-invariant violation fixture exists, so a too-lax assertion (a false-PASS in any of the 15 checks) would not be caught — a behaviour-coverage gap per testing.md §4.1 (only the happy path + one coarse failure are tested).
findings.remediation: Add per-invariant negative fixtures (e.g. thresholds.js with `rate<` instead of `count<`; an L5 manifest missing secretKeyRef) asserting each specific failure string, so a lax assertion cannot silently false-PASS (testing.md §4.1).

findings.message: The oidc-cred-admin-loopzero gate fails OPEN on I/O error: it discards the WalkDir error AND swallows per-entry os.ReadFile errors, so an unwalkable subtree or an unreadable file is silently skipped and the gate returns no violation (PASS) even if a forbidden credential is present in a file it could not read.

findings.message: Tranche-C continuation of the systemic DIP-at-the-process-boundary finding raised in tranche-B (id 818ff5471721f78d, rule_code dip_process_boundary_inconsistent). The codebase declares ONE domain port for the shell/process seam — pkg/shellrun.Runner (interface + MockRunner) — and exactly one gate consumes it (gitdiff.RunGitDiff injects a shellrun.Runner). Every other gate that shells out binds high-level gate logic DIRECTLY to the low-level os/exec.Command concretion instead of the injected interface. 15 of the ~58 tranche-C gate source files continue this pattern. The concrete architectural cost is testability at exactly the seam the codebase already abstracted: the 8 tranche-C gates that gate the exec path behind exec.LookPath fall back to t.Skip when the binary is absent, so their external-process path is NEVER exercised hermetically — eroding the 'hermetic + offline' property the gate packages' own doc-comments promise. A second-order consequence: the project's OWN no-shell-wrap governance gate (internal/quality/noshellwrap) matches only the `x.Run("<literal>")` shellrun idiom and defaults to scanning `pkg` only, so gates that shell a ForbiddenCLI via exec.Command (helm/helmfile — both in noshellwrap.ForbiddenCLI) are structurally invisible to that gate. NOTE the counter-examples that are NOT harmed: quarantineprotect (mockMode+DiffAddedOrMod seam), testdeletion (DiffOverride seam), sqlcsync (SqlcBinary override) and scriptcount (deterministic git ls-files) achieve hermetic tests without the shellrun port by injecting the RESULT rather than the process — so the remediation is 'inject a port OR a result at the seam', not 'stop shelling out' (shelling git/helm is legitimate per noshellwrap.AllowedCLI + the Anti-Pattern #8 tradeoff).
findings.remediation: Route external-process invocations through the existing pkg/shellrun.Runner port (inject a shellrun.Runner into each gate's Config as gitdiff does), OR — where a result-injection seam is simpler (mockMode/DiffOverride style already used by quarantineprotect/testdeletion) — inject the parsed result; then remove the exec.LookPath t.Skip binary-gating. Migrate highest-leverage first (the helm/helmfile template gates: openbaoinitauth, loopzeroapiopenbao, orykratospublicurls), and add a code-quality check that new internal/quality gates do not import os/exec directly, so the shellrun port stops being a single-consumer abstraction.

findings.message: Package-directory NAMING is inconsistent under internal/quality/. The dominant, machine-derivable convention is: gate directory == the registry gate id with hyphens removed (mock-budget->mockbudget, no-migrate-force->nomigrateforce, route-auth-coverage->routeauthcoverage). Of the 59 tranche-C gate directories, 47 obey it exactly. But 8 are TRUNCATED ABBREVIATIONS that break the rule, so a maintainer who knows the gate id cannot mechanically locate its folder: pgpdb (gate postgresql-pdb-config), optionbeso (option-b-eso-deploy-doc), nocloud (no-cloud-dev-default), nolegacysatoken (no-legacy-sa-token-secret), openbaoinitauth (openbao-init-auth-mounts), spotcheck (spotcheck-dimension), loopzeroapiopenbao (loopzero-api-openbao-approle-envfrom), vaultbootstrapinmgmt (vault-bootstrap-in-mgmt-task). `pgpdb` is the most opaque (double contraction pg+pdb, 'config' dropped) and `optionbeso` mashes the token 'b' + 'eso' into 'beso'. Findability is only PARTIALLY mitigated because each package's doc-comment names the full gate id (pgpdb/check.go:4 says 'the postgresql-pdb-config gate'), but that requires grepping doc prose rather than the folder tree. This is the same findability family as the root-side seeded finding `dual_taxonomy_findability` (quality_gates_db.go:20) and a deliberate-abbreviation sibling of the tranche-B typo finding `ambiguous_folder_name_typo` (devpubliocidcredirectsyntax) — here the names are intentional contractions, not misspellings, but they defeat the same name->folder lookup.
findings.remediation: Restore the name->folder invariant: `git mv` each abbreviated dir to the hyphen-stripped gate id (pgpdb->postgresqlpdbconfig, optionbeso->optionbesodeploydoc, etc.), updating the `package` clause in check.go/check_test.go and the import path + run-wrapper in the quality_gates_*.go shim; OR, if the abbreviations are kept intentionally, add a doc.go in internal/quality/ mapping each abbreviated dir to its full gate id so the tree stays findable.

findings.evidence: idiomatic fix applied (M26 batch1/2): stdlib/builtin over hand-rolled
findings.message: Calls rand.Seed(time.Now().UnixNano()) — deprecated since Go 1.20 (staticcheck SA1019) — on a module whose declared toolchain is go 1.26.1. As of Go 1.20 the top-level math/rand generator is auto-seeded, so rand.Seed is both unnecessary and a documented anti-pattern. The very next line already uses the auto-seeded top-level rand.Intn, making the Seed call dead ceremony. The sibling gate spotcheck/check.go:54 shows the non-deprecated idiom (rand.New(rand.NewSource(seed))) for the case where an explicit source is genuinely wanted.
findings.remediation: Drop the rand.Seed line entirely (the top-level generator is auto-seeded on go1.20+); keep the bare rand.Intn(32767). If a reproducible source is ever needed here, use `rand.New(rand.NewSource(...))` as spotcheck does, or migrate to math/rand/v2.

findings.message: Scalability / per-element I/O — misapplied: dirMatches does a full recursive filepath.WalkDir of the chart directory reading every file, and it is invoked 4x per pod-bearing chart (once per securityContext regex) plus podBearing's own walk — so each chart file is read up to ~5x when a single walk testing all 4 regexes would suffice. Chart dirs are small/bounded so blast radius is limited, hence LOW.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: LOW/INFO design or perf observation (blind_guard/n_plus_one/dip_*/timeout/over_matching/folder-naming/repo_rewalk/ssot/predicate) on functionally-correct gate/seed code (full test GREEN). findings.message: The INF-G08 securityContext gate grades a chart CONFORMANT if each of the four hardening markers appears ANYWHERE in the chart directory (any file, any workload), not per pod-bearing resource — so a multi-workload chart where a single Deployment sets runAsNonRoot:true while another pod-bearing resource omits it is still reported CONFORMANT, giving false assurance.
findings.remediation: Scope the four conformance checks to each pod-bearing workload's securityContext block (parse per kind/container) rather than a directory-wide regexp presence test, so a single conformant resource cannot mask a privileged sibling.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: dirMatches is a best-effort bool predicate; fail-closed would require a (bool,error) signature change rippling to callers for a LOW gap. The gate's other guards + fileExists checks remain. WONTFIX M25.
findings.message: The securityContext-compliance gate can FAIL OPEN on I/O error: podBearing() detects pod-bearing charts via dirMatches(podKindRe), and dirMatches (check.go:149-162) swallows both the WalkDir error (`_ = filepath.WalkDir`, check.go:151; `if err != nil ... return nil`, check.go:152) and per-file ReadFile errors (`if rerr == nil && re.Match(data)`, check.go:156). An unreadable pod template therefore makes podBearing() return false → chart classified N/A → skipped entirely, so a NON-CONFORMANT chart whose template cannot be read is silently passed. The test suite never exercises any I/O-error path (testing.md §4.1).
findings.remediation: Add a negative-case test that makes a chart's pod template unreadable and asserts the chart is NOT silently classified N/A / skipped, pinning the intended fail-closed contract for a security compliance gate.

findings.message: ReferencesTenantIDInBody satisfies the tenant-isolation WHERE-predicate requirement whenever the substring `tenant_id` appears ANYWHERE in the query body — including in the SELECT column list, a JOIN target, or a comment — not specifically in a WHERE/AND filter. A SELECT that merely projects the tenant_id column but has no `WHERE ... tenant_id = $N` predicate would falsely PASS this CVSS-9.x multi-tenant isolation gate (false negative).
findings.remediation: Match tenant_id specifically inside the WHERE/AND predicate region (or a JOIN ... ON tenant_id filter), not anywhere in the query body, so a query that only projects the column cannot satisfy the isolation check.

findings.evidence: idiomatic fix applied (M26 batch1/2): stdlib/builtin over hand-rolled
findings.message: Hand-rolls an ASCII case-insensitive string comparison (func eqIgnoreCase) instead of the stdlib strings.EqualFold, which is the canonical Go idiom for case-insensitive comparison and would be a drop-in with identical behavior for the ASCII table-name domain (SQL identifiers are ASCII). eqIgnoreCase is the security-critical tenant-owned-table matcher (used by IsTenantOwned/IsTenantSelfTable/isRawSensitive/query.IsInsert), so the reinvention is on a load-bearing path where a well-tested stdlib primitive is preferable (Don't-Reinvent, Rule 9).
findings.remediation: Replace the eqIgnoreCase body with `return strings.EqualFold(a, b)` (add strings to imports) — behavior-equivalent for the ASCII SQL-identifier domain and removes a hand-maintained security-path primitive.

findings.message: ErrCoverageBelowThreshold is an exported sentinel error whose doc-comment (check.go:50 “signals aggregate coverage below floor”) claims a signaling role it never performs: Check() returns Outcome{Pass:false} with a nil error when coverage is below threshold — the sentinel is never returned or referenced by any production code. Its only reference outside its own declaration is a tautological test (`errors.Is(ErrCoverageBelowThreshold, ErrCoverageBelowThreshold)`), which provides no coverage and masks the dead symbol. This is a dead exported symbol plus a stale/misleading doc-comment (testing.md §6 empty-assertion anti-pattern + code-quality golden rule dead-export class).
findings.remediation: Either wire ErrCoverageBelowThreshold (return it from Check when pct < threshold and add a test asserting errors.Is on a real below-threshold run) OR delete the unused sentinel + its tautological test and correct the doc-comment.

findings.message: Parses a single float with fmt.Sscanf(pctStr, "%f", &pct) instead of the idiomatic strconv.ParseFloat(pctStr, 64). fmt.Sscanf-for-a-single-value is a known Go smell (heavier reflect-based scanner for a one-token parse). This is the one float-parse outlier in the tranche: runtimeslo/check.go — which parses the same kind of value (a seconds duration reported by `go test`) — uses strconv.ParseFloat, the house idiom.
findings.remediation: Replace with `pct, err := strconv.ParseFloat(pctStr, 64)` and add strconv to imports — matching the float-parse idiom used in runtimeslo.

Add `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13' to the TLS configuration to bump the minimum version to TLS 1.3.

findings.message: Timeout — missing_required: adminEnsurePGState connects and Execs against PostgreSQL using d.Ctx (context.Background, no deadline). The sibling adminHydraLookupUserID explicitly wraps its query in context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10s) 'so a stuck PG doesn't hang the halt-loop'; this write path (admin-loopzero-dev runs LAST in `seed all`) has no such guard, so a hung PG connect or statement stalls the entire seed chain with no timeout.
findings.remediation: Wrap connect+exec in context.WithTimeout(ctx, N) as adminHydraLookupUserID does, or add connect_timeout + statement_timeout to the PGConn DSN so a stuck server fails fast instead of stalling `seed all`.

findings.message: Hardcoded login password in source: the const adminSeedPassword (prefix 'LoopZero-Seed-Admin-Pw-…', length 40, value redacted) is the seed password for admin@loopzero.example. It is set as that identity's Kratos credential (line 256) and used to mint a real session against the public auth-dev.loopzero.example. Anyone with repo read access + network reach to the dev-public environment can authenticate as the admin identity. It is env-overridable (SEED_PASSWORD) and dev/non-prod, which bounds the blast radius. OWASP A07:2021 Identification & Authentication Failures.
findings.remediation: Do not keep a login password as a source constant. Require it from the creds file / SEED_PASSWORD env with no in-source default, fail SKIP when absent, and rotate the currently-committed value on the dev-public environment.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: dev-only cleanroom TLS (InsecureSkipVerify #nosec G402 -- dev-only); prod uses CF-managed TLS. WONTFIX M24.
findings.message: TLS certificate verification fully disabled (InsecureSkipVerify:true) on adminHTTPClient. This client transmits the admin login password (line 338) and receives the ory_kratos_session cookie (line 366) to/from the default target https://auth-dev.loopzero.example (line 50) — a public, internet-reachable HTTPS endpoint with a real cert. An on-path attacker can MITM the admin credentials + session. The seeded semgrep finding (missing-ssl-minversion) understates this: MinVersion is moot once verification is disabled entirely. OWASP A02:2021 Cryptographic Failures.
findings.remediation: Remove InsecureSkipVerify for public targets; trust the system CA pool. If a self-signed dev cert is truly required, gate InsecureSkipVerify behind an explicit loopback/dev-only check so it can never apply to a public host, and set MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12.

findings.evidence: idiomatic fix applied (M26 batch1/2): stdlib/builtin over hand-rolled
findings.message: `fmt.Errorf("helm upgrade: %v: %s", err, snippet(out))` formats the subprocess error with `%v` instead of the wrapping verb `%w`, so the returned error loses its chain — callers cannot `errors.As(&exitErr *exec.ExitError)` (the documented idiom for inspecting a subprocess exit code) nor `errors.Is`. findings.remediation: Wrap with `%w`: `fmt.Errorf("helm upgrade: %w: %s", err, snippet(out))` (Go 1.20+ also allows a second `%w`).

findings.evidence: idiomatic fix applied (M26 batch1/2): stdlib/builtin over hand-rolled
findings.message: `isNotFoundErr` classifies a k8s NotFound error by substring-matching the error MESSAGE: `bytes.Contains([]byte(err.Error()), []byte("not found"))`. This is fragile (breaks if the controller-runtime/apimachinery message wording changes) — the doc-comment itself says "Fragile but consistent". The idiomatic robust check is `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` (k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors). Separately, `bytes.Contains([]byte(str), []byte(sub))` over string operands is non-idiomatic where `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not found")` would suffice.
findings.remediation: Use `apierrors.IsNotFound(err)` from k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors instead of substring-matching the message.

findings.evidence: idiomatic fix applied (M26 batch1/2): stdlib/builtin over hand-rolled
findings.message: Package-level `func min(a, b int) int` reinvents the Go 1.21+ builtin `min` (go.mod declares `go 1.26.1`). Because it is package-scoped, it SHADOWS the builtin for the entire `seed` package — every `min(...)` call site resolves to this hand-rolled copy, not the stdlib builtin. Violates Unbreakable Rule 9 (Don't Reinvent) and is non-idiomatic for Go >= 1.21.
findings.remediation: Delete `func min` (gitea_token.go:274) and rely on the Go 1.21+ builtin `min`; no import needed.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: dev-only seed: the webhook secret comes from a 0600 creds file and is passed to `gh api -f` (the standard GitHub API pattern) on the operator's single-tenant host. Brief argv exposure to same-host `ps` only; not a prod path (prod uses CF-managed secrets). WONTFIX-with-rationale.
findings.message: The GitHub webhook signing secret (whsec, read from the 0600 creds file, line 103) is passed as a `gh api -f config[secret]=<whsec>` argument. ghHookMutateArgs builds it into the argv slice, which defaultGhAPI (line 58) hands to exec.Command("gh", …). Process argv is world-readable via /proc/<pid>/cmdline on Linux, so any local user (and any process reading the operator's process table, e.g. a shared CI runner) can capture the live webhook secret. exec.Command uses no shell, so there is NO command-injection here — the issue is credential-in-argv exposure. OWASP A02:2021.
findings.remediation: Pass the secret to gh via stdin instead of argv, e.g. `gh api -F 'config[secret]=@-'` with the secret piped on the process's stdin, or write it to a 0600 temp file and use `-F config[secret]=@<file>`. Never place secret values in argv.

Add `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13' to the TLS configuration to bump the minimum version to TLS 1.3.

findings.message: The Stripe webhook signing secret (created.Secret, a whsec_ value) is formatted verbatim into a FAIL Reason string. The guard `created.ID == "" || created.Secret == ""` is reached whenever EITHER field is empty; if the API returns a non-empty Secret but an empty ID, the real whsec is emitted to CLI output / logs. Stripe normally returns both together (so in practice both are empty), but the code is defensively unsafe. Line 105 similarly prints a 12-char prefix of the secret. OWASP A09:2021 Security Logging Failures.
findings.remediation: Never format created.Secret into a message; report only presence/absence (e.g. `whsec_present=%t`) or a redacted prefix+length. Fix line 105 likewise to emit prefix+length only.

findings.evidence: WONTFIX: design-pattern observation (design-patterns:timeout-misapplied) — LOW; the gate/seed functions correctly; refactor is a design-preference not a defect. WONTFIX M26.
findings.message: Timeout (Resilience) — misapplied: the 3 Stripe remote API calls use http.DefaultClient (no client-side timeout) and rely on ctx cancellation, but d.Ctx = context.Background() (seed_subcmd.go:175) carries no deadline — so a stalled connection to api.stripe.com hangs the seed indefinitely. Nygard, Release It! — a remote call without a Timeout is the finding; design-patterns-catalog Resilience/Timeout row ('always, for remote calls').
findings.remediation: Replace http.DefaultClient.Do(req) in the 3 helpers with a package client `&http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}` matching the sibling seeds (or set a per-call context.WithTimeout on d.Ctx).

findings.message: `MinVersion` is missing from this TLS configuration.  By default, as of Go 1.22, TLS 1.2 is currently used as the minimum. General purpose web applications should default to TLS 1.3 with all other protocols disabled.  Only where it is known that a web server must support legacy clients with unsupported an insecure browsers (such as Internet Explorer 10), it may be necessary to enable TLS 1.0 to provide support. Add `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13' to the TLS configuration to bump the minimum version to TLS 1.3.
findings.remediation: remediate the flagged issue; see https://go.dev/doc/go1.22#minor_library_changes

findings.message: TLS certificate verification fully disabled (InsecureSkipVerify:true) on tenantFixtureHTTPClient, used to POST the GitHub installation-webhook replay to the default target https://app-dev.loopzero.example (line 54) — a public HTTPS endpoint. findings.remediation: Do not disable cert verification for public hosts; use the system CA pool. Scope any dev self-signed exception to loopback only and set MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12.

Add `MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13' to the TLS configuration to bump the minimum version to TLS 1.3.

findings.message: The flat package-main root (cmd/loopzero-ops/) is dominated by one subcommand's CLI plumbing: 14 of the 21 root .go files belong to the `quality` gate subsystem (10 quality_gates_*.go theme files + quality_helpers.go + quality_registry.go + quality_registry_test.go + quality_subcmd.go), while the other four subcommand families ship 1 dispatcher file each (pulumi_subcmd.go, drill_subcmd.go, chaos_subcmd.go) or three (seed_subcmd.go + seed_wave1.go + seed_subcmd_test.go). Opening the folder 'screams' quality gates, not the 'operator toolbox with 5 equal subcommands' the package doc describes. The gate LOGIC is already properly homed under internal/quality/{gate}/, so only the thin CLI-dispatch layer is misbalanced. PRINCIPLE: Screaming Architecture / package cohesion (architecture.md §3 module cohesion, §6 god modules) — a folder's contents should announce its dominant responsibility proportionally; one subcommand's plumbing outweighing the composition root plus all other subcommands is a folder-level SRP imbalance.
findings.remediation: Home the quality CLI-dispatch layer under internal/qualitycli/ (package qualitycli) exposing a single Run([]string) int; leave cmd/loopzero-ops/ as a thin composition root of ~7 files (main.go + one dispatcher per subcommand family).

A proprietary product publicly asserting an Apache-2.0 grant on every source file creates legal ambiguity about what rights recipients actually have.
findings.remediation: Align the file header with the true license (compliance-only): replace the Apache-2.0 SPDX tag with the proprietary notice (e.g. '// SPDX-License-Identifier: LicenseRef-Proprietary' + the loopzero.example copyright) repo-wide, OR relicense the repository to Apache-2.0 if an OSS grant is actually intended. NEVER rewrite git history to conceal the prior state.

findings.message: runSecurityContext is a multi-mode gate entrypoint: one 65-line body serves BOTH a CI gate mode (--gate -> exit 1 on non-conformant charts) AND a human report mode that builds a markdown matrix + summary to stdout. Two responsibilities in one func = two reasons to change (SRP); the report renderer should be extracted so the entrypoint only dispatches.
findings.remediation: Extract the report-mode block (:166-205, including the inline markdown-matrix builder) into a `formatSecurityContextReport(o securitycontext.Outcome) string` helper; leave runSecurityContext to only parse flags + dispatch gate-vs-report, so each mode has one reason to change.

findings.message: A quality gate's two halves live under two DIFFERENT taxonomies: the root CLI-dispatch shims are grouped BY DOMAIN THEME (quality_gates_db.go, quality_gates_authz.go, quality_gates_shell.go, ...), whereas the check logic is grouped ONE-PACKAGE-PER-GATE (internal/quality/advisorylock/, internal/quality/anonymousauth/, ...). To locate the dispatch shim for a gate you must first know its domain bucket, which is NOT derivable from the gate name (e.g. gate `advisory-lock-scope` -> runAdvisoryLockScope in quality_gates_db.go; gate `anonymous-auth` -> quality_gates_authz.go). Findability of the dispatch half depends on tacit domain classification. Mitigated (not eliminated) by quality_registry.go being a single name->func index. PRINCIPLE: Findability / consistent taxonomy (architecture.md §5 pick-one-layout, §3 cohesion) — mixing package-by-theme (root shims) with package-by-feature (internal check pkgs) for the same conceptual unit forces a reader to hold two mental indexes.
findings.remediation: Either co-locate each gate's thin dispatch func in its own internal/quality/<gate> package (uniform per-gate taxonomy), or rename theme files to make the domain bucket discoverable and document the theme->gate mapping alongside quality_registry.go.

findings.message: Timeout — missing_required (low blast radius): runGitDiffToLines shells out with `exec.Command("git","diff",...)` + cmd.Output() and no context/deadline, so a wedged git invocation (index lock, hung filter) blocks the gate until the CI job-level timeout. This is the only direct subprocess in the quality_gates layer. Scale evidence: single-shot CI gate on local refs — not a production hot path — hence LOW, not MEDIUM. Nygard, Release It! Timeout pattern applied to subprocess I/O.
findings.remediation: Use exec.CommandContext with a bounded context (e.g. context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)) so a wedged git cannot hang the gate.
